answer: Each identity must prove it runs on its own physical root of trust. At registration an agent submits a TPM quote whose endorsement key must be unique in the registry; a duplicate is rejected and the bond slashed. Because the quote binds to silicon, a farm cannot clone one machine into a thousand: it needs a thousand boxes at ~$200 each before a vote counts. The kernel of the check is cheap for one honest agent and linear in hardware for an attacker. Each new seat sends a ripple through the registry's key list, and quotes minted in the same hour show up as one umber smear on the audit trail.
